a printable answer that is neither tiny nor huge

stem: Use your calculator, set to degrees mode, to evaluate $\dfrac{{=p}\sin {=a}^{\circ}+{=q}\cos {=b}^{\circ}}{\tan {=c}^{\circ}}$. Do not round any intermediate value; give the final answer correct to $2$ decimal places.
solution: Set the calculator to degrees mode (DEG). Work out each ratio separately and keep all the digits the calculator shows; round only at the very end.
notes: Advanced: one skeleton, (p sin a + q cos b) / tan c with three different angles from all four quadrants (the book's own twist, sin 305 and tan 124 in Ex 5.2 no. 1, is the sign of a ratio beyond 90 degrees). The expression language has no sin/cos/tan, so the ratios are looked up from tables of ten-decimal values stored as integers over 10^10 (exact), computed from the true values in degrees; ANG, SIN, COS, TAN are index-aligned. Each instance is guarded: tan not near 0 or the 90/270 blow-up, no numerator cancellation, |answer| between 0.5 and 40, answer at least 0.0003 from a rounding boundary and unchanged if the ratios are first rounded to 4 dp. The stem forbids intermediate rounding. Special angles (multiples of 15 and 45 degrees) are left out so the calculator is genuinely needed. No distractors (numeric), so the catalogued degrees-mode misconception is not attached here; the worked solution's first step names degrees mode.
